description:
Create a new Excalidraw diagram from a high-level node/edge DSL (DiagramSpec).
The spec is auto-laid-out server-side. Returns the diagram id, title, and editor url.
Use this for a QUICK auto-laid-out flowchart. For a custom layout, precise styling,
or a polished/beautiful result, prefer `create_scene` (you hand-author the full scene).
Each call creates a NEW diagram and counts against your quota; to refine an existing one,
prefer regenerate_diagram / patch_elements (on quota_exceeded, trash_diagram frees a slot).

DiagramSpec (auto-laid-out node/edge DSL):
{
  "version": "1",                       // optional; only "1" is accepted
  "nodes": [                            // required
    { "id": "unique",                   // required; must be unique
      "label": "Text",                  // optional; defaults to id, "" suppresses
      "shape": "rectangle",             // rectangle | ellipse | diamond | text (default rectangle)
      "width": 140, "height": 60,       // optional; treated as a minimum
      "strokeColor": "#1e1e1e",         // optional
      "backgroundColor": "transparent", // optional
      "fillStyle": "solid",             // hachure | cross-hatch | solid | zigzag
      "group": "hardware",              // optional layout hint (not a guarantee); clusters same-group nodes; members with edges among them still span ranks
      "icon": "icon-database" }         // optional curated glyph; a curated icon id (call list_icons) drawn inside the node's top band
  ],
  "edges": [                            // optional
    { "from": "id", "to": "id",         // both must name existing node ids
      "label": "Text",                  // optional
      "arrowhead": "arrow" },           // arrow | triangle | null
    "from -> to",                       // shorthand string form, or
    "from -> to: label"                 // shorthand with a label
  ],
  "layout": { "direction": "TB" }       // TB | BT | LR | RL; optional nodeSep / rankSep
}
Caps: <=1000 nodes, <=2000 edges, label <=2000 chars, <=5000 total scene elements.

v2 — nestable containers + per-region engines (set "version":"2"). Use this for
swimlanes, layered architectures, matrices — anything where regions each want
their own layout:
{
  "version": "2",
  "containers": [                       // each container lays out its children with ONE engine
    { "id": "unique",
      "label": "Region",                // optional; shown as the frame title when frame:true
      "layout": { "engine": "grid",     // graph (auto-layout/dagre) | grid | row | column
                  "cols": 2,            // grid only (default ceil(sqrt(childCount)))
                  "direction": "TB",    // graph only: TB | BT | LR | RL
                  "gap": 40, "pad": 16 },
      "frame": true,                    // true → draw a labelled box around the region
      "children": [ { "id": "x" } ] }   // leaves (same fields as v1 nodes) or nested containers
  ],
  "nodes": [ { "id": "top" } ],         // optional top-level leaves (coexist with containers)
  "edges": [ "x -> top" ],              // GLOBAL; endpoints are LEAF ids — may cross containers
  "layout": { "direction": "TB" }       // how the top level arranges containers + top nodes
}
v2 notes: edges bind to leaf ids even across containers (arrows route between
them); the top level auto-lays-out containers + top-level nodes as a graph;
frame:true clips/moves the region as a unit. Extra caps: <=500 containers,
nesting depth <=16.

Worked example (spec):
{
  "version": "1",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "client",
      "label": "Client",
      "shape": "rectangle"
    },
    {
      "id": "api",
      "label": "API Server",
      "shape": "rectangle"
    },
    {
      "id": "db",
      "label": "Database",
      "shape": "diamond"
    },
    {
      "id": "cache",
      "label": "Cache",
      "shape": "ellipse"
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
      "from": "client",
      "to": "api",
      "label": "request"
    },
    {
      "from": "api",
      "to": "db"
    },
    {
      "from": "api",
      "to": "cache"
    }
  ],
  "layout": {
    "direction": "TB"
  }
}

See the `excaliwow://dsl/reference` resource for the full DSL reference.

folderId.description: destination folder id from list_folders (create one with create_folder); null or omitted = the root.

spec.description: diagram specification containing nodes, optional edges, and layout instructions

items.description: edge: shorthand string "a -> b" / "a -> b: label", or an object { from, to, label?, arrowhead? }
edge: shorthand string "a -> b" / "a -> b: label", or an object { from, to, label?, arrowhead? }

title.description: human-readable diagram title shown in the Excaliwow workspace and editor
